validation.rust_1_74: cargo +1.74.0 check --features mongodb,neo4j --locked passed; PostgreSQL feature separately passed earlier
validation.clippy: cargo clippy --features postgres,mongodb,neo4j --lib --test postgres_parity --test mongodb_parity --test neo4j_parity --example postgres_interop --example document_interop --locked -- -D warnings passed
validation.live_test_results: all explicitly requested live tests passed

postgres.format: Python schema-v2, NUMERIC settled amounts, blob literal escapes, permanent request/settlement tombstones
postgres.isolation: row locks acquired in deterministic scope order; clock_timestamp sampled after locks; atomic import/merge table lock
postgres.transport: convenience NoTls; connect_with_factory accepts an independently configured real postgres TLS client and is reused for heartbeats

mongodb.format: Python schema1 key/value documents and SHA256 record IDs, exact compound unique index and coordinator shape
mongodb.isolation: snapshot read concern, majority write concern, primary reads, transactional coordinator update with server $$NOW; bounded transient retries and commit acknowledgement retry
mongodb.runtime: dedicated driver worker avoids nested Tokio runtime panic; provider callbacks stay on caller thread
mongodb.upstream_default_timezone_bug: Pollard1.6 calls .timestamp() on default naive BSON UTC datetime. On Mountain Daylight host the result is 21600 seconds ahead of UTC, causing Rust window events to appear expired. Rust uses BSON epoch milliseconds. The aware oracle matches native server time.

neo4j.format: Python schema1 _PollardKV/_PollardCoordinator labels, SHA256 IDs, exact named uniqueness constraints and online RANGE indexes
neo4j.isolation: writer routing for reads and writes, shared driver bookmark manager, coordinator revision lock before server datetime.realtime epochMillis, bounded transient retries
neo4j.routing_and_bookmarks_tested: single-node real routing discovery, transactions across sessions and independent clients

limitations: Rust exact decimal amounts use rust_decimal 96-bit coefficient and scale up to28; Python Decimal supports larger values. Out-of-range values fail closed.

No dedicated MongoDB sharded-deployment, PostgreSQL failover or Neo4j multi-node failover tests were run. Native driver routing/auth/TLS mechanisms are used; standalone routing and real PostgreSQL reconnect were exercised.
PostgreSQL convenience connection uses NoTls; TLS requires caller factory. MongoDB/Neo4j database TLS has native driver support but was not exercised in these plaintext localhost service tests.

Remote traversal retains the Python shared-KV scan semantics; no remote performance advantage is claimed. Recorded performance benchmarks cover the native in-process runtime and explicitly named local stores.

test_environment.database_cleanup: PostgreSQL temporary schemas, MongoDB temporary databases, Neo4j temporary logical namespace records all removed by tests
